subject: battery
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: battery.mdl, in the place of the game's models/w_battery.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/scigun.mdl, models/w_gaussammo.mdl, models/w_squeak.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, C, D where the asset was A, B, D, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's chunky grey cell, about 18 tall and 10 across, the outline holds in every side view: a squat octagonal prism tapering to a chamfered base, with a stubby cap and handle on top. No part sticks out beyond what the brief implies, and the top handle is a small tab that stays within the outline.

M2.reason: Measured 10.3 x 10.3 x 18.4 against the brief's 10 across and 18 high: 3% off, well within 15%.

M3.reason: Brief parts checked: the grey body (present, octagonal), the glowing green panels (present on the main faces, with the frames of the panels), the hazard stripes (present as a painted band around the lower body, front and sides), and the stubby handle on top (present as a yellow striped tab on the cap). The small red indicator lights and white side strips are extra, not asked for, and nothing the brief names is missing.

M4.reason: Grey metal body with a tan tint on the frame, green glow panels, and yellow hazard paint on the lower band. Each region reads as the colour the brief names at the size shown.

M5.reason: The hazard stripes are present, but in the front and side views they read as blotchy yellow smears with dark patches rather than crisp diagonal stripes. The glow panels' mottled grain is acceptable for a glow. The stripe sharpness is clearly softer than a hazard band should be.

M6.reason: Scored 2 by rule: in the line-up of four (asset beside three Half-Life props), the judges picked the asset 0 times in four orders, and it reads as a Valve battery beside the others.

M7.reason: Stands upright on its flat-chamfered base, as the brief's resting cell does; front and back read as the same design, with the green panels on the main faces.

M8.reason: SMAK's check returned no errors. 116 triangles, below the 194 that Half-Life's most-detailed prop of its kind and size uses, so no triangle fault. Nothing open that a player can see: the underside is open in the below view, but it sits on the floor and is not visible in play.
